name: wspr
label: WSPR (HF propagation beacons)
description: WSPR (Weak Signal Propagation Reporter) is the de-facto HF propagation-sounding mode — 2-minute UTC-aligned slots, 4-FSK at 1.4648 baud in a ~6 Hz occupied bandwidth, K=32 r=½ convolutional FEC carrying a compressed callsign + 4-char Maidenhead grid + power in dBm. Beacons run a fraction of a watt and are heard worldwide. On the waterfall it's a barely-visible thin line drifting slowly inside a 200 Hz sub-band. Common dial frequencies (USB demod, 1500 Hz audio centre): 0.4742 / 1.8366 / 3.5686 / 7.0386 / 10.1387 / 14.0956 / 18.1046 / 21.0946 / 28.1246 MHz. Tune slightly off the dial (DC-spike rule); the channelizer's freq_shift_hz recovers the carrier offset. Decoded spots stream under the decoder::wspr log target every 2 minutes. Audio is teed alongside so the user can listen.
ai_notes: WSPR (HF weak-signal propagation beacons, 2 min UTC-aligned slots). Standard dial frequencies (USB demod, listen ~1500 Hz audio): 0.4742 / 1.8366 / 3.5686 / 7.0386 / 10.1387 / 14.0956 / 18.1046 / 21.0946 / 28.1246 MHz. Decodes appear every 2 min — wait ≥4 min before declaring "no traffic." Output: `tail decoder --category wspr`. Set the WsprDemod `dial_freq_hz` param to the RF dial so logged spots show the band.
